note: A draft for review. Nothing here should become a benchmark case without a person reading it: a model choosing what the benchmark contains is a model deciding what we measure ourselves against.

items.what: The text announces a corrigendum stating that interlayer binding energy values in a table required unit conversion to meV/atom and recalculation.
items.why: The excerpt is purely descriptive text reporting a correction without presenting any specific numbers, equations, or quantitative claims to evaluate.
items.text:
Corrigendum, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 28 129501 (graphite van der Waals
corrections). The interlayer binding energies -E_b in Table 1 were listed
without the necessary conversion to meV/atom, and several values taken from
previous studies have been recalculated.

items.what: The text asserts that previous PBE calculations overestimate the experimental interlayer distance c_0 by roughly 30% rather than 25.5%.
items.why: Evaluating this assertion requires accessing specific density functional theory literature values and experimental measurements, which is beyond the capabilities of the available checks.
items.text:
Corrigendum, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 28 129501. The paper stated that
previous PBE estimates for the interlayer distance c_0 are 25.5% larger than
the experimental value. They are roughly 30% larger.

items.what: The text asserts that the bulk modulus pressure derivative B_0' = 10.1 is 13.5% above the experimentally measured derivative.
items.why: Verifying this statement requires an external physical measurement that is not supplied and falls outside the capabilities of the available checks.
items.text:
Corrigendum, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 28 129501. For D3-BJ the pressure
derivative of the bulk modulus B_0' = 10.1 was described as below the
measured derivative. It is 13.5% ABOVE it.

items.what: The text asserts that the upper limit of the experimental range for the elastic constant C_33 is 38.7 GPa rather than 37.8 GPa.
items.why: Verifying an experimental measurement reported in a specific paper requires empirical literature lookup or physical experiment, which none of the available computational checks can perform.
items.text:
Corrigendum, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 28 129501. The quoted experimental
range for the elastic constant C_33 ends at 38.7 GPa, not 37.8 GPa.

items.what: The corrigendum asserts that the correct values for the improvement in interlayer binding energy are 69.5% to 1.5% rather than 56.2% to 0.6%.
items.why: Deciding which reported percentage values are physically or computationally correct requires the underlying domain-specific calculations or simulations, which none of the listed tools can perform.
items.text:
Corrigendum, J. Phys.: Condens. Matter 28 129501. The abstract reported
improvements in interlayer binding energy from 69.5% to 1.5%, while the body
of the paper reported 56.2% to 0.6%. The abstract values are the correct
ones.

items.what: The text is an erratum notice stating that an erroneous factor of 2 in an equation led to an incorrect molecular population value extracted from experimental data.
items.why: It is descriptive prose announcing an error rather than posing a quantitative problem, relation, or value to check.
items.text:
Erratum, J. Chem. Phys. 162 119901, on "Alignment of ND3 molecules in
dc-electric fields" [J. Chem. Phys. 160, 204305 (2024)]. An additional
factor of 2 was wrongly introduced into an equation, so the population
rho_{0,0} extracted from the experimental data is incorrect.

items.what: The erratum asserts that Eq. (41) of the referenced paper is missing a factor of 1/2.
items.why: Verifying this correction requires accessing and deriving the specific rate equation from the cited paper, which is beyond the scope of the available tools.
items.text:
Erratum, J. Chem. Phys. 161 019901, on "Modified Fermi's golden rule rate
expressions" [J. Chem. Phys. 159, 014101 (2023)]. There is a missing factor
of 1/2 in Eq. (41).

items.what: The text announces a correction regarding a unit conversion error that led to an overestimation by a factor of 100 and an erroneous fit in a published paper.
items.why: The excerpt is descriptive prose from an erratum notice reporting an error rather than posing or containing a checkable numerical problem or dataset.
items.text:
Correction, Environ. Sci. Technol. 57, 21927, to "Incipient Motion of Exposed
Microplastics in an Open-Channel Flow". A unit conversion error in the
calculation of a dimensionless particle parameter overestimated it by a
factor of 100, which propagated into the values plotted in Figure 6 and gave
an erroneous fit.

items.what: An erratum note explains that an axis label contained a typographical error in its unit prefix.
items.why: The text is purely descriptive editorial prose about a mislabeled graph axis and contains no calculation or quantitative claim to verify.
items.text:
Correction, Nature Communications, to "Resistive switching and its
suppression in Pt/Nb:SrTiO3 junctions". An axis label read m^4/uF^2 where it
should read cm^4/uF^2. The labels only were affected; the calculations and
conclusions were not.

items.what: The actual administered dose in the experiment was 2.46 x 10^-3 mmol/kg rather than 2.46 mmol/kg.
items.why: This is an empirical statement about an experimental measurement that cannot be verified by any of the symbolic or mathematical checks.
items.text:
Corrigendum to a biomedical Materials and Methods section. The administered
dose was given as 2.46 mmol/kg. It should read 2.46 x 10^-3 mmol/kg.

items.what: The average magnitude error resulting from the sign mistake across all 888 galaxies in the sample is 0.34 mag in J, 0.18 mag in H, and 0.15 mag in K.
items.why: Verifying these empirical averages requires the underlying observational catalog of 888 galaxies, which cannot be evaluated by the provided tools.
items.text:
Erratum to "2MTF I. The Tully-Fisher Relation in the 2MASS J, H and K Bands"
(Masters et al. 2008). A sign error was found in the application of internal
extinction and k-corrections to the magnitudes: the corrections were positive,
dimming the magnitudes, rather than negative. The average magnitude error over
all 888 galaxies in the sample was 0.34 mag in J, 0.18 mag in H and 0.15 mag
in K.

items.what: The text announces an erratum describing code corrections to Gaia proper motions and their qualitative impact.
items.why: The passage consists entirely of qualitative narrative description without specific numerical data, equations, or quantitative claims to evaluate.
items.text:
Erratum, MNRAS 511, 1224, "Revisiting the Cygnus OB associations". After
publication a small error was identified in the code processing the Gaia
proper motions. The correction produced a number of small modifications to
the numerical results, but did not change the main or qualitative results.

items.what: The note states that the spectra in version 2 were revised to include an omitted factor of omega^3.
items.why: This is an editorial change note describing a manuscript revision rather than a numerical assertion or problem.
items.text:
arXiv v2 change note, physics.chem-ph (Sep 2024). The spectra were revised to
include the omega^3 factor, which had been omitted in v1.

items.what: The material asserts that approximately 11% of surveyed papers in Nature and the British Medical Journal contained flawed statistical results.
items.why: This is an empirical research finding that requires observational data and measurement beyond the capability of the available mathematical checks.
items.text:
Reported in a scoping review of retracted clinical and translational research
(PMC11626570): a study of papers in Nature and the British Medical Journal
found flawed statistical results at a rate of about 11%.
